 Introduction 
 Jesse 
This is Jesse Pujji, and today we're breaking down the New York Times. Since its founding in 1851, the New York Times has become known as the national newspaper record through its focus on truth seeking and quality journalism. To underline that status, it has won 132 Pulitzer prizes, almost double its nearest competitor. However, the business behind the Times hasn't always been easy and it has faced several existential threats over its history, most recent of which has come from the internet and digital mediums.

 To break down the New York Times, I'm joined by Morning Brew co-founder and host of the Founder's Journal and Imposters podcasts, Alex Lieberman. It's particularly interesting to hear a new media operator dissect the heritage and evolution of one of the most story brands in this industry. Please enjoy this Breakdown of the New York Times.
